condition: Acute ischaemic stroke on a DOAC
summary: 84-year-old woman on apixaban (last dose 3 h ago) with sudden left hemiparesis, facial droop and neglect 2 h ago; NIHSS 14.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Sudden left-sided weakness and facial droop
inputs.hpi: Two hours ago, sudden left arm and leg weakness and left facial droop; she is not aware of the weakness. Atrial fibrillation on apixaban 5 mg twice daily, last dose 3 hours ago. No headache, no fall.

exam.general: Alert. Pulse 88/min irregular, BP 168/90, RR 16, temperature 36.7°C, SpO2 96%.
exam.neuro: Left facial droop, left hemiparesis (arm 1/5, leg 3/5), left-sided neglect, dysarthria. NIHSS 14. Capillary glucose 7.2.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute ischaemic stroke (right MCA) on apixaban
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Acute right MCA stroke at 2 h on apixaban (last dose 3 h ago): CT/CTA now; thrombolysis contraindicated by recent DOAC; thrombectomy if large vessel occlusion.

guideline.name: NICE NG128 — Stroke and transient ischaemic attack in over 16s: diagnosis and initial management
guideline.section: 1.1 Rapid recognition (FAST); exclude hypoglycaemia as the cause of sudden-onset neurological symptoms; suspected TIA: aspirin 300 mg immediately unless contraindicated and specialist assessment within 24 h; do not use scoring systems (ABCD2) to assess TIA risk; 1.2 imaging: non-enhanced CT immediately if thrombolysis/thrombectomy indicated, on anticoagulants or bleeding tendency; thrombolysis with alteplase within 4.5 h; thrombectomy; aspirin 300 mg after haemorrhage excluded; admit to a stroke unit
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Stroke and transient ischaemic attack in over 16s: diagnosis and initial management. NICE guideline NG128. London: NICE; 2019 (updated 2022).

guideline.name: European Stroke Organisation guidelines on intravenous thrombolysis for acute ischaemic stroke
guideline.section: Patients who took a direct oral anticoagulant within the previous 48 h: IV thrombolysis not recommended (unless specific drug levels/tests normal or dabigatran reversed with idarucizumab); mechanical thrombectomy remains an option for large vessel occlusion
guideline.citation: Berge E, Whiteley W, Audebert H, et al. European Stroke Organisation (ESO) guidelines on intravenous thrombolysis for acute ischaemic stroke. Eur Stroke J. 2021;6:I–LXII.

rationale: Anticoagulation changes the plan: immediate CT, no IV thrombolysis after recent DOAC, thrombectomy still possible (NICE NG128, ESO 2021).
